//: Every key below is optional except `commands`. Delete anything you are not changing — the defaults in .claude/harness/config.mjs are the documentation, and a config that restates them just drifts from them.

commands.//: The closing gate. Whatever your project runs when it wants to know the tree is healthy.
commands.//verifyFast: Runs at the end of EVERY turn, so it must be fast. A subset of `verify` — typecheck only, or the unit tests without the slow integration layer. Falls back to `verify` when unset, which is usually too slow.
commands.//editCheck: Runs the moment a source file is written, debounced. Must be FASTER than verifyFast. Leave it out and the edit gate never runs at all — it is off by default.

//verifyTimeoutMs: How long verify-gate waits before standing aside. A gate that hangs is worse than a gate that misses.
//source: What counts as source for 'you edited source and verified nothing'. Repo-relative globs; `**` crosses directory separators, `*` does not. Providing `include` REPLACES the default list rather than extending it.
//evidence: Which shell commands count as evidence about the health of the tree. Your `commands` are recognised automatically; add anything else you run that should be treated as verification. `match` is a JavaScript regex source string, matched case-insensitively.

verifyGate.//maxSameFailure: Attempts against ONE unchanged failure signature before the loop halts. Different failures reset the count — progress is never punished.

claimCheck.//maxBlocks: Consecutive blocks before the gate stands aside. It must never be able to trap a session.
claimCheck.//extraClaimPatterns: Additional regexes that mean 'I am asserting a gate is green'. Keep them narrow: hedged language must pass.

gates.//editCheck: Every skip here fails safe: it can only DEFER a check, never approve a broken tree, because verify-gate still runs at the end of the turn. graceMs stands down when a newer edit arrives — parallel tool calls otherwise check a half-applied refactor. windowMs skips only after a GREEN result; a red one is never suppressed.

//preflight: Entry conditions, checked BEFORE an iteration is spent. A precondition that lives as a line in a report is not a precondition: a human reading 'backend: no' stops, a loop reads it and spends its whole budget verifying loading skeletons. cleanTree and treeGreen are free and on by default; the two lists cost nothing while they are empty.

preflight.//reachable: Any HTTP response counts as up — a root that 404s is still listening. A ${env:NAME} that resolves to nothing is reported as UNSET, not unreachable: those need different fixes.
preflight.//maxConsecutiveFailures: Between-iteration failures before the run halts. One flaky response is not evidence a dependency is down; killing a four-hour run over a dropped connection is its own failure.

//locks: Which session owns which part of the tree, for repos where more than one Claude Code session shares one checkout. OFF by default. `roots` names your module boundary — empty means exact-file scope, which is the narrowest thing that is a conflict in every project. `shared` is the files every module touches by convention; without it the first session to register a module locks the shared registry and denies everyone else's correct work.

locks.//staleMs: Long enough that thinking between edits does not drop the lock, short enough that a conversation switched away from clears within one break.

//readOnlyAgents: Agents with no write access to source. They are exempt from the repair loop, because blocking them demands a fix they cannot make — and every block replays their whole context. Names match the `name:` in the agent's frontmatter.
//state: Everything the harness writes at runtime. One directory, trivial to gitignore or wipe.
